ko.text: Track closures don't overrun the buffer – trains must run on time again

top.text: Budget at least 30 at the end

name: Railway Bridge Replacement
tagline: A new structure built during weekend track closures
scope: Dismantling the old bridge and erecting a new steel structure during four track closures, when no trains run. Between closures, traffic runs and no work is allowed on the bridge.
approachText: Fixed closure windows, prescribed construction methods, rail authority oversight and a huge cost for every delay. Run purely predictively: a plan by closure, a detailed Gantt chart with a critical path, scheduling of specialists, change control and risk management.
intro: You're managing a railway bridge replacement on a main line. You get just four track closures – whatever isn't done in one has to wait for the next. And in between, trains run.

workstreams.name: Closure plan and coordination with rail operators
workstreams.why: Closures are negotiated months ahead and their dates are fixed.

workstreams.name: Dismantling the old structure
workstreams.why: The method is set by the design and the structural engineer, step by step.

workstreams.name: Fabricating and erecting the new structure
workstreams.why: The structure is fabricated to drawings in a steel shop and erected per an approved method.

workstreams.name: Welding and weld inspection
workstreams.why: Welding procedures and inspections are prescribed by standards and inspector sign-off.

workstreams.name: Track and overhead lines
workstreams.why: Follows the finished structure and must be done by the end of the last closure.

workstreams.name: Informing passengers about closures
workstreams.why: Careful: communication sounds flexible, but closure dates are fixed and notices go out within prescribed lead times.

workstreams.name: Signaling software update
workstreams.why: Careful, software: but it's a safety system approved by the rail authority. It's deployed once, verified and approved.

workstreams.name: Load test and handover
workstreams.why: The test has a standard procedure, a booked test lab date and a formal report.

phases.name: Closure 1: Dismantling
phases.goal: Cut power to the line, remove the track and lift out the old bridge span.

tasks.name: Overhead line power-off
tasks.note: No work on the bridge until the power is off.

tasks.name: Removing track on the bridge
tasks.note: Work happens right under the overhead line.

tasks.name: Cutting up the old structure
tasks.note: Cutting a structure that still has track on it? Not allowed.

tasks.name: Lifting out spans by crane
tasks.note: The crane lifts the cut-up pieces.

tasks.name: Preparing bearings on the piers
tasks.note: Work on the piers below the bridge can start as soon as the closure begins.

tasks.name: Hauling away scrap
tasks.note: Hauls away what the crane removed.

phases.name: Closure 2: Substructure
phases.goal: Repair the piers, set new bearings and prepare drainage.

tasks.name: Repairing bearing seats
tasks.note: Concrete seats the bearings will rest on.

tasks.name: Setting new bearings
tasks.note: Bearings go on the repaired seats.

tasks.name: Welding anchor elements
tasks.note: Anchors the set bearings.

tasks.name: Pier drainage
tasks.note: Independent work at the foot of the piers.

tasks.name: Survey measurement
tasks.note: Surveys the anchored bearings.

phases.name: Closure 3: Erecting the structure
phases.goal: Slide in the new spans, weld the joints and get them signed off by the inspector.

tasks.name: Sliding in new span 1
tasks.note: There's only one big crane on site.

tasks.name: Sliding in new span 2
tasks.note: Same crane as for span 1.

tasks.name: Welding the span 1 joint
tasks.note: Welds the placed span 1.

tasks.name: Welding the span 2 joint
tasks.note: Welds the placed span 2.

tasks.name: Inspector weld sign-off
tasks.note: The inspector checks all welds and arrives on day eight of the closure at the earliest.

tasks.name: Installing railings and inspection walkways
tasks.note: Installed on both placed spans.

phases.name: Closure 4: Track and testing
phases.goal: Lay the track, restore the overhead line, run the load test and hand over the bridge.

tasks.name: Track laying
tasks.note: Track goes on the finished structure.

tasks.name: Rail welding
tasks.note: Welds the laid rails.

tasks.name: Overhead line installation
tasks.note: Overhead line above the bridge, independent of the track.

tasks.name: Load test
tasks.note: Tests the finished track and overhead line. The test lab arrives on day five of the closure.

tasks.name: Rail authority acceptance
tasks.note: The bridge is accepted after a successful test.

shift.title: Rail authority tightens oversight
shift.text: After an accident on another site, the rail authority ordered: every weld in the load-bearing structure must be signed off by an inspector, and the bridge needs full quality documentation. Revealed factor: regulation and audits.
shift.lesson: When regulation increases, practices must cover it: a strict Definition of Done with quality documentation for every weld. Otherwise the inspector sends work back and closures drag on.

gate.title: Checkpoint review after two closures
gate.text: The railway administration assesses whether the project can make it through the remaining closures. How do you prepare?
gate.lesson: A checkpoint in a predictive project is about exact status against the plan: what got done in the closures, what was moved, and the risks for the next closures.

choices.text: Status vs. the closure plan, moved work, risks and a site visit
choices.feedback: The railway administration sees the exact status and approved extra crew for the next closure.

choices.text: A presentation saying everything is on plan
choices.feedback: The inspector asked about the moved work. The presentation said nothing about it.

choices.text: Cancel the checkpoint review to prepare the next closure
choices.feedback: The railway administration sent its own inspector.

events.title: Corroded pier
events.text: Once exposed, the pier turned out to be more corroded than the survey said.
events.lesson: In a predictive project, an unexpected finding goes through change control – even if it hurts. Quick fixes come back to bite.

choices.text: Change control: plan the pier repair, even at the cost of a tighter closure
choices.feedback: The repair is planned. The closure will be tight, but the bridge will last a hundred years.

choices.text: Just paint the pier and carry on
choices.feedback: The paint looks good. For now.

choices.text: Stop and wait for a new assessment
choices.feedback: The assessment arrived, but the closure lost three days.

events.title: Which crane for erection?
events.text: The crane for erecting the structure must be ordered now. A big one is pricey; a smaller one is cheaper but at the limit of its capacity.
events.lesson: For critical resources, spare capacity pays off. Skimping on them risks the whole closure.

choices.text: Order the big crane with spare capacity
choices.feedback: Expensive, but erection is a safe bet.

choices.text: Order the smaller crane
choices.feedback: Savings. The crane is at its limit.

choices.text: Decide right before the closure
choices.feedback: The decision can wait. The cranes can't.

events.title: Welders out sick
events.text: Two certified welders fell ill right before the closure.
events.lesson: Backup capacity for critical trades belongs in the risk register. Overloading the rest leads to defects.

choices.text: Call in the backup crew from the risk register
choices.feedback: The backup crew was vetted and arrived on time.

choices.text: Reshuffle work: weld only critical joints
choices.feedback: Critical joints done, the rest will wait.

choices.text: Weld with one welder on overtime
choices.feedback: The welder is working sixteen-hour days.

events.title: Rail operator wants a shorter closure
events.text: A rail operator wants the closure cut by a day for a special train.
events.lesson: A conflict over a fixed window is solved by negotiating with data and compensation. Refusing without talks comes back.

choices.text: Negotiate a detour for the special train and offer compensation
choices.feedback: The train takes a detour; the closure stays intact.

choices.text: Agree and shorten the closure
choices.feedback: The operator is happy; the closure plan is a day shorter.

choices.text: Refuse without discussion
choices.feedback: The operator left angry.

events.title: Rain during the closure
events.text: Heavy rain is forecast for the closure. Structural welds can't be done in the rain.
events.lesson: Weather is a known risk of outdoor work. A response plan (cover, reshuffled work) turns it into routine.

choices.text: Put up a tent over the welding area from the contingency reserve
choices.feedback: Under the tent, welding goes on even in the rain.

choices.text: Reshuffle work: do other tasks in the rain
choices.feedback: Some work moved; the closure is tight.

choices.text: Weld in the rain anyway
choices.feedback: The welds are done. The ultrasound test is still to come.

events.title: Minister wants an earlier opening
events.text: The construction director wants to invite the minister to the grand opening – a week earlier than the plan allows.
events.lesson: Dates promised publicly must come from the plan. A political promise without a plan comes back at the worst moment.

choices.text: Show the closure plan and set the ceremony for the real date
choices.feedback: The director isn't thrilled, but the date is realistic.

choices.text: Promise the earlier date
choices.feedback: The director is thrilled. Invitations go out.

choices.text: Refuse without explanation
choices.feedback: The director is offended.

koroze_navrat.title: Inspector finds corrosion
koroze_navrat.text: During a check, the rail authority inspector found unrepaired pier corrosion under fresh paint.
koroze_navrat.lesson: A hidden problem costs more than an admitted one. And lost trust gets added to the repair bill.
koroze_navrat.unresolvedText: The pier corrosion showed up at the first inspection after reopening.

choices.text: Admit the mistake and repair it immediately
choices.feedback: Painful but honest. The inspector approved continuing.

choices.text: Claim the pier was fine
choices.feedback: The inspector halted work and ordered a structural assessment.

choices.text: Negotiate a temporary train speed limit
choices.feedback: The bridge opens, but trains will crawl across it.

jerab_volno.title: Big crane has capacity to spare
jerab_volno.text: The big crane handles erection with room to spare. A neighboring site asks to borrow it for a day.
jerab_volno.lesson: Investing in a critical resource pays back: in certainty, and sometimes in money.
jerab_volno.unresolvedText: The big crane proved itself on later projects too.

choices.text: Rent it out for a fee on days we don't need it
choices.feedback: Part of the crane's cost came back.

choices.text: Lend it even on a day we need it
choices.feedback: The money came in, but erection stalled.

choices.text: Refuse
choices.feedback: No risk, no bonus.

vitr.title: Small crane can't handle the wind
vitr.text: A crosswind picks up while a span is being slid in. The small crane is at its limit and the operator refuses to lift.
vitr.lesson: Skimping on a critical resource costs you exactly when time is shortest.
vitr.unresolvedText: Wind pushed erection past the end of the closure.

choices.text: Wait for calm and reshuffle the work around it
choices.feedback: Safe, but the closure is now very tight.

choices.text: Risk the lift
choices.feedback: The span swung and damaged a pier. Nobody was hurt – this time.

choices.text: Rush in a big crane
choices.feedback: The big crane arrived the next day. At double the price.

jerab_pozde.title: Cranes are all booked
jerab_pozde.text: No big cranes are available for the closure. The postponed decision backfired.
jerab_pozde.lesson: Long-lead resource decisions can't be put off. Not deciding is also a decision.
jerab_pozde.unresolvedText: Erection without a suitable crane dragged on.

choices.text: Rent two smaller cranes and adjust the erection method
choices.feedback: Trickier erection, but it works.

choices.text: Pay double for a crane from abroad
choices.feedback: The crane arrived. The budget weeps.

choices.text: Postpone erection to the next closure
choices.feedback: The whole closure is practically lost.

vady.title: Ultrasound finds weld defects
vady.text: Ultrasonic testing revealed defects in welds from the last closure.
vady.lesson: Quality can't be made up with overtime or by defying the weather. Weld defects get fixed before the inspector signs off.
vady.unresolvedText: Defective welds showed up at the bridge's first inspection.

choices.text: Grind out and re-weld right away
choices.feedback: The welds are fine now. The closure is two days shorter.

choices.text: Hide the defect under paint
choices.feedback: The inspector noticed. An extraordinary inspection of the whole site follows.

choices.text: Request an extra closure for repairs
choices.feedback: Rail operators are furious, but the welds get fixed properly.

dopravce_odveta.title: Rail operator demands an audit
dopravce_odveta.text: At a public hearing, the rail operator criticizes the project and demands an independent schedule audit.
dopravce_odveta.lesson: A stakeholder nobody negotiated with finds a way – through the public and the bosses.
dopravce_odveta.unresolvedText: The dispute with the rail operator dragged on after reopening.

choices.text: Openly show the closure plan and offer regular updates
choices.feedback: The operator calmed down. The relationship is slowly mending.

choices.text: Ignore it
choices.feedback: The criticism made it into the media.

choices.text: Let the audit happen
choices.feedback: The audit confirmed the plan, but cost time and money.

ministr_prijel.title: Minister arrives, bridge isn't done
ministr_prijel.text: The minister showed up for the promised opening. The bridge isn't finished.
ministr_prijel.lesson: A promise without a plan comes back in public. Owning up and offering an alternative program beats cutting tests short.
ministr_prijel.unresolvedText: Photos of the minister on an unfinished site went all over the media.

choices.text: Hold a site tour instead of the opening and explain the plan
choices.feedback: The minister liked the tour more than ribbons and scissors.

choices.text: Cut the tests short to open in time
choices.feedback: The bridge is open without a proper test. The rail authority is furious.

choices.text: Cancel the event at the last minute
choices.feedback: The minister found out from the papers.
